title: Bands, modes and power limits
blurb: Where Technicians may use voice, CW and digital modes, how to find a band from a frequency, and the power limits.

T1B01.why: Technician voice on 10 m is **28.300 to 28.500 MHz**. Lower is CW and digital only.
T1B01.trap: 28.500 and up is beyond Technician privileges.

T1B02.why: **Any** Technician or higher may contact the ISS on VHF. No NASA approval is needed.

T1B03.why: 6 m runs **50 to 54 MHz**, so 52.525 fits.
T1B03.trap: 49.00 is just below 6 m. 28.50 is 10 m and 222.15 is 1.25 m.

T1B04.why: 146.52 MHz is in **144 to 148 MHz**, the 2 m band. Check: 300 ÷ 146.52 is about 2 m.

T1B05.why: FT8 and other digital modes are allowed in Technician segments of **10, 6 and 2 m**.

T1B06.why: On HF a Technician has phone privileges on **10 m only**.

T1B07.why: The bottom 100 kHz of 6 m (**50.0 to 50.1**) and 2 m (**144.0 to 144.1**) is CW only.
T1B07.trap: 219, 420 and 902 MHz have no such CW-only segment.

T1B08.why: Where amateurs are secondary, **non-amateur stations may be present** and you must avoid interfering with them.

T1B09.why: Display error, sidebands and drift can each push you out of the band, so stay **a little inside**.
T1B09.trap: All three reasons apply; no single one is the full answer.

T1B10.why: SSB is allowed in **at least some segment** of every band above 50 MHz.

T1B11.why: Technician HF segments allow **200 W PEP**.

T1B12.why: Above 30 MHz the limit is **1500 W PEP**, apart from specific restrictions.
